chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Abu Talib ibn al-Salt, from al-Qasim ibn al-Fudayl, who said:
I said to al-Rida (peace be upon him): 'I am sacrificed for you, a man prostrates on his sleeve due to the discomfort of heat and cold.' He said: 'There is no objection to it.'

key_terms.كُمِّهِ: his sleeve (garment part used for prostration)

ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies the flexibility in prayer postures, specifically validating prostration on the sleeve (kumm) as a valid substitute for the ground when physical discomfort from extreme heat or cold arises. It reflects the Shia jurisprudential principle of removing hardship (raf' al-haraj), demonstrating that the integrity of the prostration is maintained even when the forehead does not directly touch the earth due to necessity.
